**Mathematical diagnosis.** The defect is valid and load-bearing. The period-two map uses a single \(R_{2av}\) whether \(H_1=0\) or \(H_1=u\in\mathcal V\) with \(R_{1au}=0\); it therefore equates the later controlled response after a noninfecting exposure with the response after no prior exposure. Neither \(b\), \(q\), negative tests, nor serial serology identifies this equality. Consequently, the claimed exact fiber and sharpness currently apply only to an unvalidated no-priming submodel.

**Chosen repair.** Introduce explicit period-two response coordinates after each prior exposure and a scalar mismatch sensitivity parameter \(\delta\in[0,1]\). This retains a finite linear response-type model, the external exposure margins, and the original unprimed controlled-challenge estimand.

**Exact directive to proposer.**

> Replace `ass:stable-noninfecting-history-response` and its serology justification as follows. Enlarge the latent type with \(R^{[u]}_{2av}\in\{0,1\}\), \(u\in\mathcal V_0\), where \(u=0\) is the period-two controlled response after no period-one exposure and \(u\in\mathcal V\) is the response after a period-one exposure to \(u\) that did not infect. Set
> \[
> \tilde g_{1av}=1\{h_1^a=v\}r_{1av},\qquad
> \tilde g_{2av}=1\{h_2^a=v\}r^{[h_1^a]}_{2av}
> \Bigl(1-\sum_w\tilde g_{1aw}\Bigr).
> \]
> For a disclosed \(\delta\in[0,1]\), impose for every \(a,u,v\), \(u\in\mathcal V\),
> \[
> \sum_s1\{h_1=u,r_{1au}=0\}
> 1\{r^{[u]}_{2av}\ne r^{[0]}_{2av}\}x_s
> \le
> \delta\sum_s1\{h_1=u,r_{1au}=0\}x_s .
> \]
> Thus \(\delta\) bounds the fraction of noninfected exposés whose later controlled response is altered by that exposure; \(\delta=0\) recovers no priming and \(\delta=1\) permits unrestricted priming. Replace \(\mathcal P\) by the resulting \(\mathcal P_\delta\), use \(\tilde g\) in the \(b\)-constraints, and define the unchanged target’s period-two risk using \(r^{[0]}_{21v}\). Restate exact compression, sharpness, positivity, and dual results pointwise in prespecified \(\delta\), and report the identified-set/sign conclusion over a scientifically justified \(\delta\)-range. Preserve \(q\) as the external exposure margin; do not substitute case-strain frequencies. State explicitly that routine negative tests or serial serology do not identify a small \(\delta\); absent a randomized/controlled validation substudy, \(\delta\) is a sensitivity parameter.

**Field-tier assessment.** Yes, the field-tier claim remains plausible if this sensitivity-indexed fiber is carried through the substantive theorem chain. The finite-type sharpness machinery survives, while the repair directly encodes rather than assumes away the scientific crux.

> Strengthen `prop:sensitivity-range-report` into the paper’s sensitivity-range theorem. Prove directly from `ass:bounded-noninfecting-exposure-priming` that, for \(0\le\delta_1\le\delta_2\),
> \[
> \mathfrak M_{\delta_1}\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\delta_2},\qquad
> \mathcal P_{\delta_1}\subseteq\mathcal P_{\delta_2},\qquad
> \Theta_{I,\delta_1}\subseteq\Theta_{I,\delta_2}.
> \]
> Since every nonempty closed \(\mathcal D\subseteq[0,1]\) contains \(\bar\delta=\max\mathcal D\), conclude exactly
> \[
> \bigcup_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\mathfrak M_\delta=\mathfrak M_{\bar\delta},
> \qquad
> \Theta_I^{\mathcal D}=\Theta_{I,\bar\delta},
> \]
> so the closure and continuum supremum currently used in `prop:sensitivity-range-report` are unnecessary, and every uniform range-sign or range-coverage audit reduces to the single largest admissible \(\delta\). When a strict sign holds at a baseline value, also define the sharp priming breakdown point as the smallest \(\delta\) for which the opposite-side LP becomes feasible; prove attainment by compactness/nesting, dual certificates below the threshold via `thm:common-history-sign-dual`, and a compatible counterlaw at the threshold via `thm:exact-history-compression`. **(3) Panel / novelty / class verdicts.**

- **Panel:** causal inference / partial identification / vaccine-methodology panel; not a generic optimization or asymptotic-theory paper.
- **Novelty:** **field-tier plausible but borderline**, conditional on making the maximal-\(\delta\)/breakdown theorem the headline and demoting the definitional compression and standard LP machinery. Otherwise the work reads as a substantial model-specific assembly of known tools.
- **Class:** **distinct and nonnested; no transfer currently established.** Janvin–Stensrud assume well-defined isolation/challenge interventions, exposure necessity, a treatment/exposure structure, an exposure-effect inequality, and exposure exchangeability; their paper expressly warns that a survivor cross-world equality is not a sufficient justification. The present class instead uses external margins, arbitrary exposure–response dependence, common exposure histories, and a mismatch sensitivity restriction. The \(K=1,\delta=0,q=1\) calculation recovers one risk inclusion, not their law class. [Janvin–Stensrud primary text](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.01336)
- Perényi–Stensrud use an FFRCISTG longitudinal class with \(U,Z\), time-to-event exchangeability and positivity, exposure necessity, no cross-infectivity, a covariate-invariant exposure ratio, and scaled-new-infection proportionality. Their assumptions 7–11 already point-identify \(CSE_k\); restating the current sharp-set result over that class would reproduce their identification result, not strengthen it. [Perényi–Stensrud primary text](https://arxiv.org/html/2408.07560)
- A converse could transfer upward only after constructing two witness laws in an explicitly embedded subclass satisfying the relevant published base hypotheses. Current compatible-law witnesses are not shown to do so. Therefore the go/no-go receipt should say **GO for the distinct external-margin sensitivity model; NO class-equivalence, inclusion, or published-class transfer claim.**
